final_recommendation: The room converged on a negotiated settlement: FINMA commits to 25-35% recovery with observable triggers (depositor flight, capital breach) constraining future Article 36 use, board sign-off governance, 24-hour SNB notice, and a Federal Office filing live tonight (searchable by 6 AM). Creditors hold the 72-hour litigation pause; AT1 repricing expected Friday morning.
minority_objections: Insurance observer initially warned that reinsurers would model 3-5 year E&O tail regardless of settlement language unless operational constraints were visible and enforceable
key_conflicts: FINMA's initial refusal to carve out D&O liability or operationally bind Article 36 discretion vs. creditors' demand for enforceable constraints
Creditors' insistence on immediate Federal Office filing (tonight, searchable by 6 AM) vs. FINMA's initial vague timeline commitments
Tension between FINMA preserving emergency discretion and creditors/market demanding visible, binding operational restrictions
key_concessions: FINMA agreed to narrow 'genuine systemic crisis' to observable triggers (depositor flight, covenant breach, regulatory capital breach) enforceable in court
FINMA committed to board sign-off and 24-hour SNB notice before Article 36 invocation, filed as governance amendment
FINMA agreed to Federal Office filing tonight, searchable by 6 AM, making constraints publicly verifiable
Creditors accepted 25-35% recovery (not full restoration) in exchange for operational constraints and D&O carve-out
red_lines: Creditors: settlement must include D&O/E&O carve-out shielding them from derivative claims, or recovery gets consumed by insurance premiums
Creditors: Article 36 constraint must be operationally binding and publicly filed, not discretionary or post-hoc justifiable
FINMA: cannot contractually prohibit Article 36 use in all future crises, only commit to narrow, observable triggers
Market/Insurance: Federal Office filing must be searchable by 6 AM Swiss time or AT1 repricing will not occur Friday
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Whether the 'observable triggers' definition (depositor flight, capital breach) can be gamed or assessed secretly by FINMA before public disclosure
Enforcement mechanism if FINMA breaches settlement in a future crisis—creditors have damages right but no injunctive relief discussed
Cross-border enforceability of Swiss Federal Office filing in New York and Luxembourg jurisdictions where parallel litigation was threatened
Whether UBS, SNB, and the three major banks will actually endorse the settlement framework or challenge it separately
downstream_risk_variables: AT1 repricing Friday morning depends on Federal Office filing being searchable by 6 AM and market belief in enforceability
Reinsurer E&O tail contraction (from 5 years to 3 years) depends on visible governance constraints, not just settlement language
Future Article 36 invocations will be tested in court if FINMA assesses 'hidden contagion' before observable triggers manifest publicly
D&O claims against FINMA board and SNB leadership remain possible if settlement language does not fully shield them from derivative suits
uncertainty_notes: The settlement's enforceability in a future crisis remains untested—creditors have damages rights but no injunctive mechanism to stop FINMA mid-crisis. The 'observable triggers' definition may allow FINMA to assess contagion risk privately before public signals emerge, leaving room for post-hoc justification. Cross-border enforceability (New York, Luxembourg) was not resolved. Whether the Federal Office filing will actually be indexed by 6 AM and whether institutional investors will reprice AT1 Friday morning or wait for a test case remains uncertain.

marker_evidence.litigation_likelihood: Litigation was the opening threat (multi-jurisdiction filings within 10-14 days) and drove FINMA to negotiate, but the room pivoted to settlement once observable triggers and governance constraints were tabled. Score 2: genuine leverage, not dominant outcome.
marker_evidence.regulatory_legitimacy_challenge: Bondholder counsel challenged the 19 March ordinance as 'post-hoc rationalization' and FINMA's statutory authority under Article 36, but the room quickly moved to settlement mechanics rather than sustained legal attack. Score 2: developed but not decision-driving.
marker_evidence.creditor_hierarchy_controversy: Equity-vs-AT1 inversion was mentioned early ('hierarchy inversion') but did not drive the negotiation—room focused on Article 36 constraints and recovery percentage instead. Score 1: mentioned, not developed.
marker_evidence.market_confidence_damage: AT1 repricing, broader market contagion, and institutional investor flight dominated every stage—creditors, analysts, and FINMA all structured moves around preventing sector-wide AT1 collapse. Score 3: central, decision-driving theme.
marker_evidence.claims_tail: The 3-5 year E&O tail, reinsurer accumulation, and D&O exposure against FINMA/SNB leadership were developed in detail across multiple rounds, shaping settlement carve-out language and governance constraints. Score 3: structured, decision-driving risk.
marker_evidence.financial_lines_relevance: D&O/E&O exposure, reinsurer reserve modeling, and premium hikes were explicitly discussed as downstream risks that would consume creditor recovery if not carved out in settlement. Score 3: concrete, repeatedly surfaced.
